evidence: eBible.org current catalog lists these English and multilingual resources.
eBible.org metrics report 1,543 Bible translations and 1,024 languages with freely redistributable translations for September 2026.
Open Bibles repository confirms public-domain/free-license status for its listed files.
Current eBible.org translation metrics expose concrete minority-language resources including Auhelawa, Abau, Abureni, Achagua, Achi, Achuar-shiwiar, and Adioukrou.
Open Translation Bible currently lists English, Hindi, Persian, French, and Norwegian Bokmål releases under CC BY-SA 4.0.
Additional open/public-domain repositories provide distinct translation manifestations and licensing metadata; repository mirrors are not counted as separate works.
Open.Bible currently exposes 945 openly licensed Bible translations.
DBL currently reports text, audio, signed, and Braille Scripture resources; media/artifact manifestations are tracked separately from text works.
New manuscript and knowledge-artifact discovery paths include CSNTM, Open Dead Sea, Patristic Text Archive, scholarly editions, and digitized book/scanned-artifact catalogs.
Bible discovery now explicitly models books, translations, manuscripts, artifacts, audio, video, Braille, signed Scripture, maps, and scholarly/patristic knowledge resources.
Current Find-A-Bible catalog reports 6,722 Bibles across 7,929 languages and 244 countries.
Current Open.Bible catalog reports 945 openly licensed Bible translations.
Dead Sea Scrolls Digital Library exposes fragment-level image and metadata browsing by site, language and content, including biblical and non-biblical compositions.
Current Open Translation Bible repository lists releases through Swahili and additional languages; each language is captured as a separate edition candidate.
BOOST: added concrete textual corpora, manuscript witnesses, linguistic databases, patristic corpora, ancient translations, and textual-criticism datasets rather than only catalog-level records.
Current research repositories expose Peshitta OT/NT, BHSA Hebrew, Dead Sea Scrolls, Targums, Ephrem, Syriac manuscripts, lexicons and cross-corpus linguistic data.
Current Targum corpus demonstrates the desired work/edition/instance model: 223 works, 334 editions and 651 instances across five languages, with book coverage and provenance.
Open Bible Data currently has nearly 1.3 million generated pages with parallel, interlinear, dictionary and cross-reference layers.
Open Dead Sea currently reports 53,568 transcribed source-text lines and 53,479 published English machine-draft reading-aid lines.
Open Scriptorium combines scripture, deuterocanon, Talmud, historical Jewish literature and patristic/post-patristic voices with verse-level cross-referencing.
Surface break: node-level knowledge objects now include scrolls, fragments, lines, words, verses, morphology, syntax, lexical data, parallels, manuscript metadata and scholarly encodings.

Surface break continued: added linguistic annotation corpora, Greek critical-text resources, Coptic/Syriac corpora, manuscript image/transcription infrastructure, historical Christian corpora, semantic metadata and cross-reference graphs.

Precision surface-break evidence: STEPBible exposes TAHOT, TAGNT, lexicons, proper-name entities, versification, morphology codes and manuscript-meaning variant datasets; MACULA Hebrew contains syntax trees, word senses, semantic roles and participant referents; NTVMR exposes a large Greek NT manuscript research environment; Coptic SCRIPTORIUM publishes multiple annotation formats.

Deep object expansion validated against current source documentation: STEPBible exposes translator tags, tagged OT/NT corpora, lexicons, concept groups, proper-name entities and versification; MACULA exposes nested syntax, lowfat query structures and word-level records; Coptic SCRIPTORIUM exposes token, morpheme, entity, identity, treebank, manuscript-linked and aligned-translation layers.

Fresh source verification: MACULA Greek contains syntax trees, morphology, senses, semantic frames, participant referents, synonyms, mappings and adjunct types; STEPBible TAGNT explicitly tracks per-word edition membership, positional/meaning variants, lexical/morphological tags, plus TIPNR people/places/things and relationships; Coptic SCRIPTORIUM release data includes Bible corpora, papyri, apocrypha, patristic works and Magical Papyri with machine-readable annotation.

Blast-off expansion: moved across Syriac, Greek, Latin, early English print, Jewish textual graph, NT manuscript witnesses, cross-reference edges and semantic Bible metadata. The graph now explicitly models authors, works, volumes, manuscripts, pages, witnesses, people, places, themes, events and relationship edges.

Fresh verification: CoptOT documents manuscript cataloguing, standardized codex naming, diplomatic/critical editions, translations, Sahidic corpus and citation/lexicographic tools; CSNTM exposes manuscript classifications and feature metadata plus high-resolution images; Princeton Geniza Project publishes thousands of searchable transcriptions and research datasets; Biblissima IIIF records expose manuscript authority, codicology, language, date, shelfmark, contents and image manifests.

Fresh surface break: CoptOT explicitly exposes manuscript images, metadata API, page-level TEI transcriptions, collation rules, citations, inscriptions/ostraca, critical editions and translations. Sinai Manuscripts Data Portal currently exposes 401 text units across Arabic, Syriac, Greek, Coptic, Georgian, Armenian, Ge'ez and other languages, with biblical, Gospel, apocryphal, commentary, hymnal and lectionary genres. Kyprianos publishes downloadable manuscript and text tables updated July 2026. Coptic SCRIPTORIUM v6.3 reports over 2.38 million words and new biblical, patristic, hagiographic and fragment corpora.
